title: Exploring The World Of Lucid Dreaming

questions.q: What premise makes lucid dreaming possible?
a: The same mind creates both waking and dream experience
Dreams are broadcast from an outside source
Sleep erases nearly all waking memory
Only certain people can recall dreams
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the waking and dreaming states share one mind.

a: Asking yourself often during the day whether you are dreaming
Testing your alarm clock before bed each night
Waking at a set time to recall your dreams
Writing down your goals before sleeping
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the habit carries over into your dreams.

questions.q: What distinguishes a wake-initiated lucid dream?
a: You stay conscious as you fall asleep
You wake up suddenly inside a dream
You dream about waking up several times
You sleep without remembering anything
questions.why: Lesson 2 says WILD means falling asleep without losing awareness.

a: The transitional state between waking and sleeping
A technique for recalling dreams later
A kind of recurring nightmare
The deepest stage of sleep
questions.why: Lesson 2 defines it as the limbo between wakefulness and sleep.

questions.q: Which benefit of lucid dreaming does the summary describe?
a: Practicing skills in dreams can improve real ability
It removes the need for normal sleep
It makes nightmares impossible
It replaces therapy for most people
questions.why: Lesson 3 cites studies on imaginary practice and real skills.
